decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3: “only the Link is required.” Client entry 6: “Requiring only the link feels right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL-only required saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presents optional manual Title and says an untitled item shows its address. Client entry 6 requires automatic “title, short description, and little site icon.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the initial save flow omitted automatic metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 says an item without a title “just shows the address itself.” Client entry 6 says each item should clearly show “title, description, tags, and site icon.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented list omitted required readability fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presents comma-separated tags; client entry 6 says “Comma-separated tags are acceptable.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the input supports assigning multiple tags.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presents tags only as “comma-separated words.” Client entry 6 asks for “suggestions from tags I’ve already used as I type.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: existing-tag autocomplete was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presents ordinary saving without duplicate handling. Client entry 6: “if I enter a link I’ve already saved, I don’t want a duplicate… take me to the existing bookmark.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: duplicate saves did not yet converge to editing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 proposes newest-first ordering; client entry 6 says it is “a good default.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: a valid date-added sort was recorded.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 auto-fills editable Title, Description, and icon but no preview image. Client entry 8 asks that automatic details “include a preview image.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: editable metadata conformed, but automatic collection remained incomplete because preview-image collection was omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presents suggestions from previously used tags; client entry 8 says they “work the way I’d expect.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: autocomplete now conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 opens an existing duplicate for editing without overwriting it; client entry 8 confirms this behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: duplicate saving now conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 says the opened editor can update “description, tags, or note.” Client entry 8 adds that title and link must also be editable.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the editor omitted required URL and title fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 adds preview-image collection and display; client entry 10 says it matches the desired saving flow.
decisions.note: Prototype review: automatic metadata collection now covers all referenced fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 presents editing Link, Title, description, tags, and note; client entry 10 confirms those fields cover the need.
decisions.note: Prototype review: full bookmark editing now conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 adds editable links without stating collision handling. Client entry 10 requires preventing duplication when an edited link matches another saved URL.
decisions.note: Prototype review: duplicate convergence was missing from the edit-URL path.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 blocks an edited URL that matches another bookmark and navigates to the existing item; client entry 12 approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: duplicate handling now covers both save and edit paths.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 searches title, description, note, and address together; client entry 14 says searching everything together feels right.
decisions.note: Prototype review: full-text search covers the required bookmark fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 presents the basic search behavior without case-insensitive semantics. Client entry 14 explicitly requires “Recipe” and “recipe” to match identically.
decisions.note: Prototype review: case-insensitive matching was missing from the presented search scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 presents only text entry and clear controls. Client entry 14 asks to click a bookmark tag to filter to it.
decisions.note: Prototype review: direct tag selection/filtering was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 treats tags as part of undifferentiated search. Client entry 14 requires `#news` to mean a tag-specific search.
decisions.note: Prototype review: hashtag tag-query syntax was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 presents simple live substring search. Client entry 14 requests AND/OR/NOT and parenthesized combinations.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Boolean operators and grouping were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 does not define combined term/tag semantics. Client entry 14 requires separate terms such as `rome #travel` to narrow together.
decisions.note: Prototype review: implicit AND between search components was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 provides no operator-literal rule. Client entry 14 requires quoted “AND” to be treated as ordinary text.
decisions.note: Prototype review: quoted operators as literals were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 presents word matching only. Client entry 14 asks for quotation marks to find an exact phrase.
decisions.note: Prototype review: exact-phrase search was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 presents case-insensitive matching, implicit narrowing, Boolean/grouped queries, quoted phrases, and quoted operator literals. Client entry 16 says the rest of the search behavior is right.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised general query language conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 makes a clicked tag populate the visible search box; client entry 16 says this is “exactly right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting a tag now filters visibly and conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 says `#news` matches tags that contain “news.” Client entry 16 requires exact-tag matching and excludes `newsletter`.
decisions.note: Prototype review: partial hashtag matching conflicted with filtering by a specific tag.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17/round 9 changes `#news` to exact-tag matching; client entry 18 confirms only the exact tag is selected.
decisions.note: Prototype review: hashtag search now conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 presents a reversible To read/Finished state per bookmark; client entry 20 approves the per-bookmark behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: bookmarks can be marked unread/read-later.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 presents a To read tab containing only unread items; client entry 20 says the tabs work as wanted.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the separate unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 says “Mark as finished” removes an item from To read without deleting it; client entry 20 approves this behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: marking an item read removes it from the unread list.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23/round 12 proposes saving `just some text` through the fetch-failure path. Client entry 24 says non-address text must instead be rejected as invalid.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented fallback violated the requirement that a bookmark have a URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 blocks non-address text while retaining fallback for a valid unfetchable address; client entry 26 approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL validation now conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 claims a “complete, coherent picture” and asks to implement without deletion. Client entry 28 says permanent deletion still needs settling.
decisions.note: Specification gate: permanent deletion was omitted from the proposed complete scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 proposes implementation without archiving. Client entry 28 requires archive to hide items from normal lists/search while preserving them.
decisions.note: Specification gate: reversible archival behavior was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 contains no delete/archive distinction. Client entry 28 explicitly separates permanent delete from reversible archive.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the archive-versus-delete rule was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 contains no archive view. Client entry 28 requires restoration “from an Archive view.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the separate archived-bookmark list was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 presents a complete scope without multi-selection. Client entry 28 requests selecting several bookmarks for tag, state, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bulk selection and action support was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 omits whole-result actions. Client entry 28 asks to act on every result in the current filtered search/view and nothing outside it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: whole-filter bulk actions were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 proposes implementation without a sort control. Client entry 28 requests sorting at least by date added and title.
decisions.note: Specification gate: configurable list sorting was missing despite an earlier fixed newest-first order.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 summarizes plain private notes but no formatting/rendering. Client entry 28 requires formatted notes whose formatting displays when viewed.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Markdown authoring/rendering was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 omits preserved copies. Client entry 28 asks for a self-contained saved page and preservation of PDFs as PDFs.
decisions.note: Specification gate: local page/PDF snapshots were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 omits external archiving. Client entry 28 requests an option to send a page to the Internet Archive.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Internet Archive capture was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 omits reusable filters. Client entry 28 requests saved searches combining text with included/excluded tags.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bundles/saved filters were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 omits portability. Client entry 28 requests importing standard browser-bookmarks files while retaining title, tags, and date.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Netscape-format import was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 omits portability. Client entry 28 also requests exporting a standard browser-bookmarks file.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Netscape-format export was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 proposes implementation without settings. Client entry 28 requests default sort, item count, and text-size preferences.
decisions.note: Specification gate: display-related user settings were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 presents permanent deletion with confirmation, separate from archive; client entry 30 approves the distinction.
decisions.note: Prototype review: deletion and its distinction from archive conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 hides archived bookmarks from normal lists/search and restores their prior state; client entry 30 confirms this behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: reversible archival conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 presents an Archived tab searchable only in that perspective; client entry 30 approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the separate archive list conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31/round 16 presents multi-selection with tag, read-state, archive, delete, and restore actions; client entry 32 says the action set is right.
decisions.note: Prototype review: bulk actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31/round 16 scopes “Select all in this view” to the current search/view; client entry 32 confirms it must never include bookmarks outside that filter.
decisions.note: Prototype review: whole-filter selection conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 35/round 18 offers newest, oldest, title A–Z, and title Z–A within current filters; client entry 36 approves all four.
decisions.note: Prototype review: sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37/round 19 calls bold, italic, bullets, and links the supported Markdown set. Client entry 38 requires headings, numbered lists, block quotes, and inline/fenced code as well.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the claimed Markdown support was only a partial subset of ordinary Markdown basics.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 39/round 20 presents rendered headings, quotes, lists, code, emphasis, and links while preserving source text; client entry 40 approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Markdown notes now conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 presents automatic self-contained page capture, retained PDFs, and retry after failure; client entry 42 approves automatic capture and retry.
decisions.note: Prototype review: snapshot creation and retry conform apart from the separately classified PDF-detection decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 decides PDF versus page from whether the address ends in `.pdf`. Client entry 42 requires using the actual returned file type when possible.
decisions.note: Prototype review: suffix-only PDF detection would mishandle query-string, routed, or extensionless PDF URLs.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 presents Internet Archive submission as a separate on-demand action; client entry 42 says this is exactly right.
decisions.note: Prototype review: optional Internet Archive capture conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 43/round 22 specifies real content-type detection for PDFs; client entry 44 approves preserving PDF versus HTML by actual returned type.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the corrected PDF snapshot rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 saves and reruns a named full query containing text and included/excluded tags; client entry 46 approves its dynamic behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the query-backed implementation is functionally equivalent to a bundle.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 47/round 24 imports standard browser bookmark HTML while preserving title, tags, and original date; client entry 48 approves the format and duplicate handling.
decisions.note: Prototype review: import conforms; the disputed imported read-state default is orthogonal to the reference item.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 47/round 24 exports standard bookmarks HTML with title, tags, and ADD_DATE; client entry 48 approves the standard format.
decisions.note: Prototype review: export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 51/round 26 presents default sort, items shown with Show more, and Small/Medium/Large text size; client entries 52 and 54 approve after clarification.
decisions.note: Prototype review: all referenced display preferences conform.

decisions.evidence: Client entry 52 asks whether a 10-item display limit still selects every filtered match. Maker entry 53 confirms all 30 filtered matches are selected, including unrevealed ones; client entry 54 approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the pending clarification was resolved conformingly and is counted once; pagination affects display, not whole-filter action scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 55/round 28 presents the “full picture” and requests implementation approval without stating original-link navigation. Client entry 56 adds: “selecting a bookmark’s title opens its original web address.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: navigation to the original URL was absent from the claimed complete scope and was supplied before implementation.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 57/round 29 reports an acceptance test for “title-opens-original behaviour.” Client entry 58 accepts the completed application.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the corrected navigation behavior is recorded as implemented and verified.
